Which Roman god, king of the gods, is the equivalent of the Greek god Zeus?
Which Carthaginian general crossed the Alps with elephants to attack Rome?
What was the underfloor heating system used in Roman baths called?
Which Roman emperor allegedly, according to legend, set fire to Rome in 64 AD to rebuild it to his liking?
Which painter is considered the father of Impressionism?
What is the name of the famous Paris museum that houses the largest collection of Impressionist works?
True or false: Impressionism was born in Italy.
What is the Claude Monet painting that gave the movement its name called?
Which Impressionist painter is famous for his paintings of ballet dancers?
Which artist is known for his paintings of Mont Sainte-Victoire?
questions.a: Paul Cézanne (although he is often classed as a post-Impressionist).

questions.q: Which painter created “Luncheon of the Boating Party”?
What is the first name of the woman Impressionist painter Morisot?
Which Impressionist painter spent the last years of his life in Tahiti?
questions.a: Paul Gauguin (although he is also considered a post-Impressionist).

questions.q: Which painter, close to the Impressionists, is famous for his Moulin Rouge posters?
What does the acronym “AK” stand for in AK-47?
Which country is the world's largest manufacturer and exporter of firearms?
What is the name of the standard assault rifle of the US Army since the 1960s?
questions.a: The M16 (or its variants such as the M4).

questions.q: Which famous firearms brand created the 1911 model?
What is the part of the weapon that holds the ammunition before it is loaded into the chamber called?
What is the name of the Austrian semi-automatic pistol widely used by law enforcement?
What is the main difference between an assault rifle and a sniper rifle?
questions.a: The assault rifle is designed for automatic or burst fire at short to medium range, while the sniper rifle is designed for single-shot, long-range fire.

questions.q: Which country is known for having invented gunpowder?
What is the name of the first truly automatic machine gun, invented in 1884?
What is the standard NATO caliber for assault rifles?

cards.subject: Think you're good at French cheeses?

questions.q: Which cheese is famous for its holes?
Which region is the birthplace of Camembert?
Which blue cheese, often called the king of cheeses, comes from Aveyron?
True or false: Brie is a hard cheese.
Which cheese is traditionally used in tartiflette?
Which of these cheeses is a washed-rind cheese: Munster or Beaufort?
Which small puck-shaped goat cheese comes from the Loire region?
Which uncooked pressed cheese comes from Cantal and has the same name as the département?
Which cheese, often associated with Savoyard fondue, is produced in Savoie and Haute-Savoie?
What is the name of the Corsican sheep's or goat's milk cheese, known for its strong smell?
questions.a: Brocciu (or Casu Marzu, although the latter is from Sardinia, it is often associated with Corsica).

questions.q: Which room in the house is generally dedicated to preparing meals?
Which appliance is used to wash dishes automatically?
True or False: Pillows are mainly used in the bathroom.
Which object, often located in the entryway, is used to hang coats?
What is the main function of a doormat?
questions.a: To wipe your feet before entering.

questions.q: What is the room called where you generally find a sofa and a television?
Which object, often found in the living room, is used to put down cups and magazines?
Which appliance is used to suck up dust from floors?
What is the main function of a nightstand?
questions.a: To put things next to the bed (lamp, book, alarm clock).

questions.q: Which object, often found in the bathroom, is used to look at yourself?
Which ancient Greek physician is considered the “father of medicine”?
Which French scientist developed the first rabies vaccine in 1885?
Which infectious disease, once deadly, was eradicated worldwide in 1980 thanks to vaccination?
What is the name of the Scottish physician who invented the stethoscope in the 19th century?
questions.a: René Laennec (he was French, the question contains an error; René Laennec was Breton).

questions.q: Which major medical advance, discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928, revolutionized the treatment of bacterial infections?
Which British physician pioneered vaccination using the cowpox virus (vaccinia)?
Which woman scientist won two Nobel Prizes for her work on radioactivity, which had important medical applications?
Which South African surgeon performed the first successful human heart transplant in 1967?
Which term refers to the ancient practice of drilling a hole in the skull to treat various ailments?
Which international organization, founded in 1948, aims to bring all peoples to the highest possible level of health?
What is the name of the world's most venomous snake, found in Australia?
Which plant, famous for killing Socrates, produces a poison called coniine?
Which chemical element, with the symbol As, was historically used as a poison in the Roman Empire?
What is the name of the famous poison extracted from the castor bean?
Which fish, considered a luxury dish in Japan, can be deadly if not prepared properly because of its tetrodotoxin?
Which spider, recognizable by the red hourglass on its abdomen, has a very potent venom?
Which odorless, colorless gas is called the “silent killer”?
Which marine animal, often found in Australia, has venom capable of killing a human in minutes?
What is the name of the toxin produced by the poison dart frog of South America?
What is the specific antidote given in case of cyanide poisoning?
questions.a: Hydroxocobalamin (or vitamin B12a) and amyl nitrite/sodium thiosulfate.

questions.q: Which cocktail is made with rum, mint, lime and soda water?
What is the main ingredient of a Margarita, along with Cointreau and lime juice?
Which Italian cocktail is made of Prosecco, Aperol and soda water?
True or False: The Cosmopolitan contains vodka.
Which Cuban cocktail is made with rum, cola and lime juice?
Which classic cocktail is made of gin and dry vermouth and is often garnished with an olive?
Which ingredient gives the Negroni cocktail its red color?
Which Brazilian cocktail is made of rum, coconut cream and pineapple juice?
questions.a: The Piña Colada (originally from Puerto Rico, but popular in Brazil; the question contains a small error).

questions.q: Which bourbon, lemon juice and sugar syrup cocktail is often garnished with a maraschino cherry and an orange slice?
Which cocktail is made of gin, lemon juice, sugar syrup and blackberry (blackberry liqueur)?
Which black-and-white animal, often found in North America, is famous for its foul smell?
Which vegetable, often used in cooking and said to repel vampires, can give bad breath?
True or False: Durian is a fruit known for its pleasant smell.
questions.a: False (it is known for its very strong, often unpleasant smell).

questions.q: Which French cheese, often associated with the North, is famous for its strong smell?
Which flower, often called the “corpse flower”, gives off a smell of rotting flesh to attract pollinating insects?
Which chemical, often added to natural gas to detect leaks, smells like rotten eggs?
Which bird, resembling a vulture, has a defense mechanism of vomiting a foul substance on its predators?
Which houseplant, often called the “money plant”, can give off a smell of rotten fish if it lacks water?
What is the name of the foul-smelling substance produced by the glands of certain mammals, like beavers, to mark their territory?
Which mineral, often found in volcanic hot springs, gives off a smell of sulfur or rotten eggs?
What is the capital of Spain?
What is the capital of Sweden?
What is the capital of Greece?
True or False: Geneva is the capital of Switzerland.
What is the capital of Hungary?
Of which European country is Helsinki the capital?
Which city is the capital of Poland?
What is the capital of Slovakia?
Of which European country is Ljubljana the capital?
What is the capital of Estonia?
Which mental disorder is characterized by episodes alternating between depression and mania?
Which mental illness, often associated with hallucinations and delusions, affects the perception of reality?
Which anxiety disorder is characterized by sudden, intense panic attacks?
What is the acronym for post-traumatic stress disorder?
Which eating disorder is characterized by episodes of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors (vomiting, excessive exercise)?
Which personality disorder is characterized by a persistent pattern of instability in interpersonal relationships, self-image and emotions?
Which neurodevelopmental disorder, often diagnosed in childhood, is characterized by difficulties in communication and social interaction?
Which anxiety disorder is characterized by intrusive thoughts (obsessions) and repetitive behaviors (compulsions)?
Which term refers to a mood disorder characterized by persistent sadness, loss of interest and lack of energy?
Which personality disorder is characterized by a lack of empathy, manipulative behavior and disregard for the rights of others?
Which Italian dessert made with coffee, mascarpone and ladyfingers is famous worldwide?
Which tube-shaped Sicilian pastry is filled with sweetened ricotta?
Which Piedmontese dessert is a cooked cream, often served with a red berry coulis?
True or false: Panettone is a dessert originating in Rome.
Which dry, crunchy almond biscuit comes from the city of Prato in Tuscany?
questions.a: Cantuccio (cantucci in the plural, or biscotti).

questions.q: What is the name of traditional Italian ice cream, often denser and less fatty than classic ice cream?
Which spongy Neapolitan cake is often soaked in rum or limoncello?
Which Venetian dessert is made of candied fruit, nuts and honey, often eaten at Christmas?
Which chocolate and almond cake, originating from the island of Capri, contains no flour?
Which shell-shaped Neapolitan pastry is filled with ricotta, semolina and candied fruit?
Which office tool is used to cut paper and has two crossed blades?
Which kitchen tool is used to cut a pizza into equal slices?
True or False: A scalpel is a tool used by surgeons to make incisions.
Which sharp object is used to shave a beard closely?
Which tool, often used by lumberjacks, is used to cut wood?
Which instrument is used to trim nails precisely?
Which tool, made of a toothed blade, is used to cut metal or wood?
Which sharp tool is used by gardeners to trim hedges and shrubs?
Which small cutting tool, with a retractable blade, is often used to open cardboard boxes?
What is the name of the curved single-edged sword traditionally used by Japanese samurai?
Who are the two American brothers credited with the first powered, controlled airplane flight in 1903?
Which ocean did Charles Lindbergh cross solo and nonstop in 1927?
True or False: Concorde was the first supersonic airliner to enter commercial service.
questions.a: False (it was the Soviet Tupolev Tu-144).

questions.q: What is the name of the double-deck, four-engine airliner made by Airbus, the largest passenger aircraft in the world?
Which American aviator was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean?
Which world conflict saw the first large-scale use of fighter planes and bombers?
Which German engineer designed the first operational jet aircraft, the Messerschmitt Me 262?
Which Soviet supersonic transport aircraft, nicknamed “Concordski”, flew before Concorde but met a tragic fate?
Which French pilot, a World War I ace, gave his name to a famous tennis tournament?
Which American aerospace company produced the famous 747 airliner, nicknamed the “Jumbo Jet”?
Which long straight sword was the main weapon of European knights in the Middle Ages?
What is the name of the traditional Scottish dagger, often worn in the sock?
Which curved blade, originating in the Middle East and North Africa, is characterized by its crescent-shaped blade?
Which type of war axe, often double-headed, was used by the Franks and the Vikings?
Which Japanese weapon, shorter than the katana, was often worn as a pair with it by samurai?
Which dagger with a triangular or cruciform blade, designed to pierce armor or chain mail, was popular in the Renaissance?
Which long spear, topped with an axe blade and a spike, was the favored weapon of Swiss and German foot soldiers in the Renaissance?
What is the name of the short, broad sword used by Roman legionaries?
Which bladed weapon, originating in India, is characterized by an H-shaped grip and often a curved or wavy blade?
Which type of sword with a long, narrow, flexible blade was mainly used for thrusting during Renaissance duels?
Which yellow spice, from the rhizome of a plant, is the main ingredient of curry?
Which red spice, often sold as a powder, is made from dried peppers or sweet chilies?
Which spice, from the inner bark of a tree, is often used in desserts like gingerbread or cinnamon rolls?
True or False: Black pepper, white pepper and green pepper come from the same plant.
questions.a: True (only the stage of ripeness and the processing differ).

questions.q: Which expensive red-orange spice is extracted from the stigmas of a crocus flower?
What is the name of the small black seed, often used in Indian and Middle Eastern cooking, with a slightly bitter, earthy taste?
Which star-shaped spice has a pronounced anise flavor and is often used in Asian cooking?
Which pungent spice is extracted from the root of a plant of the mustard family, often served with sushi?
Which very aromatic bud, originating in Indonesia, is often stuck into an onion to flavor broths?
Which spice, from the red covering of the nutmeg, is often used in spice blends like garam masala?
Which fabric item is used to dry your body after a shower or bath?
Which product is generally used with a brush to clean teeth?
True or False: Shampoo is designed to clean the skin of the body.
Which appliance is often used to dry wet hair?
Which small object on a stick is used to clean ears (although doctors advise against it)?
Which basin, generally fixed to the wall, collects water for washing your hands or face?
Which product is often used to prevent body odor, especially under the arms?
Which accessory is used to untangle and style hair?
Which plumbing fixture sprays water on the body for washing while standing?
Which rough or spongy object is used to scrub the skin and remove dead cells?
questions.a: An exfoliating glove (or shower pouf/exfoliating sponge/loofah).

questions.q: Which country was torn apart by a civil war between 1936 and 1939, pitting Republicans against Nationalists led by Franco?
Which African civil war, which began in 1994, led to a genocide that killed about 800,000 people in 100 days?
Which country had a civil war between 1861 and 1865, pitting the Union in the North against the Confederate States in the South?
True or False: The English Civil War (1642-1651) led to the execution of King Charles I and the proclamation of a republic.
Which civil war took place in Russia from 1917 to 1922, mainly pitting the “Reds” (Bolsheviks) against the “Whites” (anti-Bolsheviks)?
Which conflict ravaged Lebanon from 1975 to 1990, involving multiple religious and political factions as well as foreign interventions?
In which Asian country did a long civil war pit the communist forces of Mao Zedong against the nationalists of Chiang Kai-shek?
Which war, which broke out in 1991, led to the breakup of Yugoslavia into several independent states?
questions.a: The Yugoslav Wars (or the Bosnian/Croatian war, etc.).

questions.q: In which Central American country did a civil war pit the government against the FMLN guerrillas from 1979 to 1992?
Which civil war, which began in 2011 in the wake of the Arab Spring, involves the regime of Bashar al-Assad and multiple rebel groups?
Which beer, generally light in color and mild in taste, is the most consumed in the world?
Which Irish dark beer is famous for its creamy head and roasted taste?
Which beer, often associated with Germany, is brewed with a high proportion of wheat malt?
True or false: IPA (India Pale Ale) is a type of heavily hopped beer.
Which Belgian beer, often flavored with cherry, is called Kriek?
Which type of beer, often high in alcohol, is traditionally brewed by Trappist monks?
Which dark beer, originating in London, is often considered the ancestor of stout?
Which spontaneously fermented beer, from the Senne valley in Belgium, is often sour and non-carbonated?
Which term refers to a blond or amber top-fermented beer originating in the Cologne region of Germany?
Which beer, originating in the city of Plzeň in the Czech Republic (Bohemia), gave its name to a very popular style of pale lager?
Which winter item is used to glide on snow with both feet fixed on a single board?
Which yellow fruit, often eaten by monkeys, is famous for its peel that you can slip on (in cartoons)?
True or False: Soap is a product that tends to slip when it is wet.
Which animal, often found in Antarctica, slides on its belly over the ice to move faster?
Which clear, viscous liquid is often used to reduce friction between mechanical parts?
Which rectangular board is used to glide on water and catch waves (ridden standing up)?
Which natural phenomenon, often invisible, makes roads extremely slippery in winter?
Which legless reptile moves by sliding (or slithering) along the ground?
Which object slides along a zipper to open or close it?
What is the name of the small plastic or wooden sheet used to slide on snow, often called a “snow shovel” sled?
Which Frenchman is credited with inventing photography in 1826 with his “View from the Window at Le Gras”?
Which photographic process, producing a unique image on a silver plate, was presented by Louis Daguerre in 1839?
Which American company democratized photography with its “Brownie” camera and slogan “You press the button, we do the rest”?
True or False: The first permanent color photograph was made in the 19th century.
Which British scientist invented the first negative-positive process, the calotype, allowing images to be reproduced?
Which type of photography, using light to create images without a camera, was popularized by Man Ray (the “rayographs”)?
Which American photographer is famous for his black-and-white landscapes of the American West, especially Yosemite National Park?
Which Japanese company was the first to market a digital camera for the general public in 1989?
questions.a: Fujifilm (with the Fujix DS-X, although Kodak invented the first prototype).

questions.q: Which term refers to a photograph of oneself, often taken by holding the camera at arm's length?
Which British physicist made the first permanent color photograph in 1861 using three color filters?
Which synthetic drug, often called “ecstasy” or “MDMA”, is popular in the electronic music scene?
Which powerful and highly addictive stimulant is often called “crystal meth” or “ice”?
Which substance, originally developed as an anesthetic, is often used as a dissociative drug and called “Special K”?
True or False: LSD is a synthetic opiate.
Which powerful hallucinogenic drug, synthesized by Albert Hofmann, is often taken on small blotter papers?
What is the name of the synthetic drug of the cathinone family, often called “bath salts” or “flakka”?
Which synthetic drug, often called “GHB” or “G”, is sometimes used as a “date rape drug”?
Which extremely potent synthetic opioid painkiller is often involved in overdose crises in North America?
What is the acronym for phencyclidine, a dissociative drug often called “angel dust”?
Which synthetic drug, derived from amphetamines, was widely used as an appetite suppressant in the 1960s before being banned?
Which long, thin pasta, often served with bolognese sauce, is the best known in the world?
Which bevel-cut tube-shaped pasta, often served with arrabbiata sauce, has a name meaning “quills”?
Which pasta, whose name means “little ribbons”, looks like flat spaghetti?
True or False: Gnocchi are traditionally made with potato.
Which butterfly- or bow-tie-shaped pasta is often used in cold salads?
Which type of filled pasta, often square or half-moon-shaped, has a name meaning “little turnips”?
Which long, flat pasta, wider than tagliatelle, is often served with rich, creamy sauces?
Which short, twisted pasta, often used in baked dishes, has a name meaning “little springs”?
Which filled pasta shaped like a small ring or navel comes from the Emilia-Romagna region?
Which small pasta shaped like a grain of rice or melon seed is often used in soups?
Which farm animal, known for its snout, likes to roll in the mud to cool off?
Which farm bird, raised for its meat and eggs, is famous for its morning call?
True or False: Sheep are raised mainly for their milk.
questions.a: False (for their wool or meat, although some breeds are dairy).

questions.q: Which farm animal, often used to pull plows, is the result of crossing a donkey with a mare?
Which large flightless running bird, sometimes raised on farms, lays the biggest eggs in the world?
Which small furry animal, known for its long ears, is sometimes raised for its meat (cuniculture)?
Which ruminant animal, often with horns and a little beard, is reputed to be able to climb trees and eat almost anything?
Which aquatic bird, raised for its foie gras or meat, makes a sound called quacking?
What is the female turkey, raised for its meat, called?
Which animal, resembling the llama but originating in the Andes, is sometimes raised on farms for its very soft wool?
Which Soviet cosmonaut was the first man to travel into space in 1961?
Which NASA space program sent the first men to the Moon in 1969?
True or False: Laika, the first dog in space, survived her trip.
questions.a: False (she died a few hours after launch).

questions.q: What is the name of the first artificial satellite launched into Earth orbit by the USSR in 1957?
Which Soviet astronaut was the first woman to fly in space in 1963?
What is the name of the space telescope launched in 1990 that revolutionized our understanding of the universe?
Which international space station, launched in 1998, has been continuously occupied since 2000?
Which car-sized NASA rover landed on Mars in 2012 to explore Gale Crater?
Which American astronaut made the first US suborbital flight in 1961?
Which space probe, launched in 1977, became the first human-made object to enter interstellar space?
Which viral disease caused a worldwide pandemic from 1918 to 1920, often called the “Spanish flu”?
questions.a: Influenza A (H1N1), or the Spanish flu.

questions.q: Which virus, transmitted through blood and body fluids, destroys the immune system and causes AIDS?
True or False: Bubonic plague, responsible for the Black Death in the 14th century, is caused by a virus.
questions.a: False (it is a bacterium, Yersinia pestis).

questions.q: Which infectious disease, mainly affecting the lungs, is caused by Koch's bacillus?
Which virus, causing severe hemorrhagic fevers, has caused several deadly outbreaks in West and Central Africa?
Which parasitic disease, transmitted by anopheles mosquitoes, is one of the leading causes of death in sub-Saharan Africa?
Which coronavirus emerged in late 2019 and caused a worldwide pandemic?
Which disease, once common in children and causing skin rashes, has been nearly eradicated thanks to vaccination (MMR)?
Which term refers to a serious infection caused by a spiral-shaped bacterium (spirochete), often sexually transmitted and able to reach the brain in an advanced stage?
Which viral disease, affecting the central nervous system and often fatal once symptoms appear, is transmitted by the bite of an infected animal?
Which light shoe, often made of canvas or leather, has a braided rope sole?
Which Converse sports shoe is famous for its star on the ankle and its rubber sole?
questions.a: The Chuck Taylor All Star (or Converse All Star).

questions.q: Which shoe, often made of rubber, is designed for use in water and shares its name with a reptile?
True or false: Pumps are flat shoes.
Which laceless shoe, often leather, was popularized by American students and sometimes has a tassel on top?
Which type of shoe, rising above the ankle, is often worn for hiking or work?
Which shoe, made of a simple sole held by a Y-shaped strap, is very popular in summer?
What name is given to elegant men's dress shoes characterized by closed lacing?
Which classical dance shoe, reinforced at the toe, allows dancers to stand on the tips of their toes?
Which wooden-soled shoe, of peasant origin, is traditionally associated with the Netherlands and certain regions of France?
Which small metal object, often attached to a keyring, lets you open a door?
Which visual protection accessory, often resting on the head or nose, is frequently misplaced?
True or False: Socks are often lost, especially after going through the washing machine.
Which portable communication device is often frantically searched for in pockets or bags?
Which small object lets you light a cigarette or a candle?
Which object, often containing money and credit cards, is a particularly stressful thing to lose?
Which small device lets you change the TV channel without getting up?
Which hair accessory, often made of fabric or elastic, seems to disappear mysteriously?
Which accessory used in winter to protect the hands is often lost, leaving its owner with an odd one?
Which object, used to protect from the rain, is frequently forgotten on public transport or in restaurants?
Which punctuation mark ends a declarative sentence?
What part of speech is the word “apple” in the sentence “I eat an apple”?
True or False: In the sentence “He sings well”, “well” is an adjective.
Which verb mood is used to express an order, advice or a prohibition (e.g. “Come here!”)?
What is the function of the phrase “in Paris” in the sentence “He lives in Paris”?
Which coordinating conjunction links elements of the same kind or function and expresses addition?
What is the past participle of the verb “write”?
Which type of subordinate clause is introduced by a relative pronoun (who, which, that, whose, where)?
In the sentence “The cat that I see is black”, what is the function of the pronoun “that”?
What is the figure of speech that attributes human characteristics to an animal or a thing called?
What is the act of eating human flesh (when done by humans) called?
Which famous American serial killer, nicknamed the “Milwaukee Cannibal”, murdered and dismembered 17 young men?
True or False: Cannibalism has never been practiced for survival reasons in modern history.
questions.a: False (e.g. the crash of Flight 571 in the Andes).

questions.q: Which fictional character, a psychiatrist and cannibal, is the protagonist of the film “The Silence of the Lambs”?
Which British explorer was killed and, reportedly, eaten by natives in Hawaii in 1779?
questions.a: James Cook (legend says he was eaten, but historians think his body was prepared according to local funeral rites).

questions.q: Which isolated Amazonian tribe was reputed for its ritual endocannibalism practices at funerals?
Which fatal neurological disease, similar to mad cow disease, spread among the Fore people of Papua New Guinea because of cannibal rituals?
Which famous Japanese criminal killed, dismembered and ate a Dutch student in Paris in 1981, before being declared unfit to stand trial?
Which indigenous people of New Zealand were accused, sometimes wrongly, of cannibalism by the first European explorers?
Which term refers to cannibalism practiced within one's own group or tribe, often for ritual reasons?
Which pasty substance, often sold in a tube or jar, is used to join two pieces of paper?
Which transparent ribbon, adhesive on one side, is often used to wrap gifts?
True or False: Honey is a substance that can be very sticky.
Which small square of pre-glued paper, invented by 3M, is used to leave repositionable notes?
Which sweet food, often pink or blue, made by spinning melted sugar, is famous for being very sticky?
Which resinous substance, often exuded by pines and firs, is very sticky?
Which type of adhesive dressing, often flesh-colored, is used to protect small wounds?
Which malleable paste, often used by plumbers to make watertight seals, has adhesive properties?
Which very strong adhesive tape, often silver-gray or black, is reinforced with cloth?
What is the name of the hook-and-loop fastening system, made of two strips (one with tiny hooks, the other with soft loops)?
What is the French equivalent of “I am”?
Which verb tense is used to express an action in progress (e.g. I am eating)?
True or False: Adjectives agree in gender and number in English.
Which auxiliary is used to form questions in the present simple (e.g. Do you like apples?)?
questions.a: Do (or Does for the 3rd person singular).

questions.q: What is the most common plural ending for nouns in English?
questions.a: Adding an “s” at the end of the word.

questions.q: What is the past participle of the irregular verb “to go”?
Which relative pronoun is used to refer to a person (e.g. The man ___ is standing there)?
How do you express possession with a proper name (e.g. Paul's book)?
questions.a: By using the Saxon genitive ('s): Paul's book.

questions.q: Which modal verb is used to express ability or possibility (e.g. I can swim)?
In the sentence “If I had money, I would buy a car”, which type of conditional is used?
questions.a: The second conditional (unreal hypothesis in the present).

questions.q: Which machine, invented during the French Revolution, was used to behead the condemned?
In which North American country is the death penalty still practiced in several states?
True or False: The European Union requires the abolition of the death penalty for all its member states.
In what year was the death penalty abolished in France (under President François Mitterrand)?
Which method of execution, consisting of administering a cocktail of drugs, is the most commonly used in the United States today?
Which device, using electric current to execute a condemned person, was invented in the late 19th century?
Which Italian Enlightenment philosopher wrote the famous treatise “On Crimes and Punishments”, arguing for the abolition of the death penalty and torture?
Which international non-governmental organization, a Nobel Peace Prize winner, actively campaigns against the death penalty worldwide?
In which Asian country do executions by hanging, often kept secret until the last moment, draw international criticism?
questions.a: Japan (the question says Japan, although other Asian countries also carry out secret or hanging executions).

questions.q: Which old method of execution, consisting of tying the condemned to a wheel to break their bones, was common in early modern Europe?
Which cut of meat is ground to make ground beef patties?
questions.a: Various cuts (often shoulder, neck or chuck).

questions.q: Which tender, elongated cut of beef is often considered the most noble and the most expensive?
Which thick, marbled cut, ideal for grilling and taken from the upper part of the animal, is it?
True or False: Chuck (paleron) is an ideal cut for quick grilling.
questions.a: False (it is a cut for slow simmering or braising).

questions.q: Which large cut of beef, including the rib bone, is often shared among several people at a barbecue?
questions.a: The bone-in rib steak (côte de bœuf).

questions.q: Which beef cut, from the abdomen, is very flat and stringy and needs short, high-heat cooking?
questions.a: The flank steak (bavette), or skirt/hanger steak.

questions.q: Which gelatinous cut of beef, from the leg or shoulder, is essential for a good pot-au-feu or beef bourguignon?
questions.a: The shin or the topside (the shoulder or chuck are also accepted).

questions.q: Which beef cut, called “T-bone” in English, combines part of the tenderloin and the strip separated by a T-shaped bone?
Which beef cut, located near the tenderloin, is tender but cheaper, and often used for roasts?
What is the meat from the beef jaw called, famous for its tenderness after long slow cooking?
Which object filled with feathers or foam do you put under your head to sleep?
Which wobbly, melt-in-the-mouth dessert, often fruit-flavored, is very popular in American hospitals?
True or False: A mattress is generally designed to be as hard as stone.
Which spongy treat, often white or pink, is traditionally toasted over a campfire?
Which fermented dairy product, sold in small cups, is known for its creamy, soft texture?
Which foam toy, often shaped like animals, is designed to be squeezed to relieve stress?
Which colorful modeling clay has been popular with children for decades (famous brand)?
Which white Asian food with no strong taste, made from curdled soy milk, comes in a very soft “silken” version?
Which fruit, when very ripe (or overripe), becomes extremely soft and sweet, ideal for making bread or cakes?
questions.a: The banana (or the very ripe persimmon, the avocado, the pear).

questions.q: Which spongy, porous substance, often artificial, is used to make cleaning sponges or cushions?
What is the fastest land animal in the world?

questions.q: Imposed Scolaire theme
questions.a:
The team rates itself out of 10 on the topic. If the team doesn't like the proposed question, it may change the question on the same topic once.
In case of a wrong answer, the team will draw a new "It's superb" card on the next turn.

questions.q: Free choice of theme
questions.a:
2 questions of your choice on the same topic. Points add up for correct answers.
If neither answer is correct, the team moves back to the nearest "Not good at all" space.

questions.q: Imposed Mature theme
questions.a:
If the team answers correctly in under 10 seconds, the points are doubled.
If it takes more than 10 seconds, the usual game rules apply.
In case of a wrong answer, the team will draw a new "It's superb" card on the next turn.

questions.q: Free choice of theme
questions.a:
With a correct answer, the team moves forward by its self-rated score and hands a "Not good at all" card to each opposing team (to be used on their very next turn).
In case of a wrong answer, the team will draw a new "It's superb" card on the next turn.

questions.q: Free choice of theme
questions.a:
Answer the 10 questions of the drawn topic.
You move forward one space per correct answer.

questions.q: Imposed Mature theme
questions.a:
Answer the 10 questions of the drawn topic.
You move forward one space per correct answer.

questions.q: Imposed Mature theme
questions.a:
Points doubled for a correct answer to a question rated 6/10 or higher.
If you choose a question below 6/10, the usual game rules apply.
In case of a wrong answer, the team will draw a new "It's superb" card on the next turn.

questions.q: Free choice of theme
questions.a:
Once the topic is known, the team tries to answer a question 8, 9 or 10. In case of a wrong answer, the team may choose any question it wants on the same topic.
In case of a wrong answer to the second question, the team will draw a new "It's superb" card on the next turn.

questions.q: Imposed Scolaire theme
questions.a:
If the team answers correctly a question rated above 5/10, it moves forward that many spaces, as usual. The other teams then move back to the nearest "Not good at all" space.
In case of a wrong answer, the team will draw a new "It's superb" card on the next turn.
If a question rated 5/10 or lower is chosen, the usual game rules apply.

questions.q: Free choice of theme
questions.a:
Answer question 10 and win the game.
In case of a wrong answer, the team may choose another question on the same topic and move forward that many spaces, as usual.
In case of another wrong answer, the team will draw a new "It's superb" card on the next turn.
